sharing.unavailable: This browser can't seal or sign keys yet, so this can't be done here. Do it from a Kemlock app.
space.keysPending.title: This space waits for its keys to be replaced
space.keysPending.body: Changes to the space and its collections are paused until its owner replaces the keys from an app that can re-encrypt every item.
space.error.keysPending: The space waits for its keys to be replaced, so it can't be changed yet.
space.error.fingerprint: That fingerprint isn't the one of the member's keys. Don't confirm: start again.
space.error.lastOwner: A space needs at least one confirmed owner.
space.error.wrongState: That isn't possible in the member's or the space's current state.
space.error.staleKey: A collection's key was replaced meanwhile. Reload the space and try again.
space.error.notVerified: {name}'s keys can't be traced to a confirmation this browser can check, so no key was sealed to them. Compare their fingerprint and confirm them again.
space.keysPending.chained: A member who held its keys is gone, so changes are paused until the keys are replaced. Replacing them here seals every item of the affected collections again under new keys, all in one step, which can take a while in a large space. If it can't be done in one step, a Kemlock app does it.
space.keysPending.elsewhere: Only a member who can edit the affected collections, from a browser that holds their keys or from a Kemlock app, can replace them.
space.error.replaceTooLarge: This space is too large to replace its keys from the web vault: use the Kemlock app. Nothing was changed.
space.error.replaceNoManifest: This space has no signed list of its items to say which are to be sealed again, so its keys can't be replaced from the web vault: use the Kemlock app. Nothing was changed.
space.error.replaceUnreadable: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} of this space can't be opened in this browser, so its keys can't be replaced from the web vault: use the Kemlock app. Nothing was changed.
space.keys.sealing: Sealing {total, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} again…
space.reseal.title: {count, plural, one {# item is} other {# items are}} still under an old key
space.reseal.body: Until they are sealed again under the current key, they can't be read or changed. Only the browser session that replaced the keys, or a Kemlock app that still holds the old key, can do it. After a reload this page can't: it tries with what this session holds.
space.reseal.done: {rewritten, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} sealed again.
space.reseal.stuck: {stuck, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} can't be sealed again here: this browser no longer holds the old key, can't edit it, or the signed list of items doesn't have it as it is. A Kemlock app or the device that replaced the keys can.
space.keys.done: The keys are replaced: {rewritten, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} sealed again.
space.keys.held: {held, plural, one {# item stays} other {# items stay}} held: the signed list of items doesn't have it as it is, so it may be a removed member's write and is not sealed again. Someone with edit on its collection writes it again to release it.
space.chain.unsupported: Moving a collection and restoring a removed member aren't available in the web vault: invite the member again, or use a Kemlock app.
space.error.chained: This space's keys can't be opened in this browser, so nothing can be signed for it. Reload it, or change it from a Kemlock app.
space.error.chainRefused: The space's rules don't allow that change ({reason}).
space.error.chainConflict: Someone else changed the space at the same moment. Reload it and try again.
space.error.noAccount: There is no account with that email.
space.error.unchecked: This space can't be checked, so it can't be changed.
space.chain.unchecked.title: This space can't be checked
space.chain.unchecked.body: Its signed history didn't verify here ({reason}), so no key of the space is opened, nothing is sealed to anyone, and nothing about it is shown as checked. Tell an admin if this keeps happening.
space.chain.unreachable.body: Its signed history couldn't be read just now, so no key of the space is opened and nothing about it is shown as checked. Try again in a moment.
space.chain.contact.title: Check this space before trusting it
space.chain.contact.compare: Ask {name} to read out the numbers their app shows for their account (Settings, Account security), and check they match these:
space.chain.contact.pick: The person who added you can't be used for this check any more. Pick an owner, ask them to read out the numbers their app shows for their account, and check they match:
space.chain.contact.none: No owner can be used for this check yet. Ask an owner to make a change in the space, then try again.
space.chain.contact.label: Fingerprint of {name}'s keys
space.chain.contact.warning: Different numbers mean someone else's key is in the way. Don't go on: the space's keys stay closed.
space.list.title: Spaces
space.list.lede: Spaces share items between people. Each has its own key, which a member only receives after someone has compared their fingerprint with theirs.
space.list.none.title: No spaces yet
space.list.none.body: Make one below, or wait for an invitation from someone who has one.
space.new.title: New space
space.new.hint: The space key and the first collection's key are made in this browser and sealed to you. The server keeps names only as ciphertext.
space.new.name: Space name
space.detail.meta: You are {role} · {members, plural, one {# member} other {# members}} · {collections, plural, one {# collection} other {# collections}}
space.detail.notConfirmed: You haven't been confirmed in this space yet, so its names and keys stay closed to you. Ask an admin to confirm you.
space.members.title: Members
space.inviteLink.copied: Link copied. Whoever opens it accepts the invitation for this account, so hand it only to the person invited.
space.inviteLink.manual: Your browser would not copy it. Copy the link below. Whoever opens it accepts the invitation for this account, so hand it only to the person invited.
space.inviteLink.noInvitation: There is no Bitwarden invitation to copy for this member.
space.inviteLink.forbidden: Only an owner or admin can copy this link, and only an owner for the invitation of an admin or manager.
space.inviteLink.accepted: This member has already accepted, so there is no link to copy.
space.keys.compare.title: Compare a member to open this space
space.keys.compare.body: The keys of this space were sealed by someone this browser can't trace yet. Ask {name} to read out the numbers their app shows for their account, and check they match. Once they do, this browser trusts what {name} sealed and confirmed, and opens the space.
space.keys.legacy.title: Some keys were sealed before keys were signed
space.keys.legacy.body: This browser can't tell who sealed them, so it trusted them the first time it saw them. Ask an owner or admin to confirm you again, or to replace the keys, so they are sealed and signed by a member you can check.
space.pin.title: Compare {name}
space.pin.body: Ask {name} to read out the numbers their app shows for their account, and check they match. Once they do, this browser trusts the confirmations {name} made, and the keys of the members they confirmed can be traced:
space.revoke.title: Revoke {name}?
space.revoke.body: They lose access at once. Everything they could open counts as seen, and the space's keys must be replaced.
space.remove.title: Remove {name}?
space.remove.body: They leave the space for good. Everything they could open counts as seen, and the space's keys must be replaced.
space.offboarded.title: {name} no longer has access
space.offboarded.none: They could open no collection with items in it.
space.offboarded.exposed: They could open {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} in {collections, plural, one {# collection} other {# collections}}. Change those passwords.
space.offboarded.keys: The space now waits for its keys to be replaced.
space.invite.title: Invite someone
space.invite.permission: What they can do in those collections
space.confirm.title: Confirm {name}
space.confirm.body: Confirming seals the space key to {name}'s own keys. Ask them to read out the numbers their app shows for their account, and check they match:
space.confirm.inconsistent: This browser's two ways of working out the fingerprint disagree. Don't confirm.
space.confirm.unreadable: {name}'s key bundle can't be read, so it can't be confirmed.
space.confirm.warning: Different numbers mean someone else's key is in the way. Don't confirm.
space.collections.title: Collections
space.groups.title: Groups
space.grants.title: Who opens what
space.grants.none: Nobody has been granted a collection yet.
devices.approval.title: {name} is asking to sign in as you
devices.approval.from: From {ip}, {ago}. Approve only if you started it and it shows this phrase:
devices.approval.phraseLabel: The phrase worked out from the request's key
devices.fingerprint.title: Your account's key fingerprint
devices.fingerprint.hint: When you approve a new device, it shows this fingerprint and asks you to compare. Continue there only if it is exactly the same as this one. If it differs, the server is handing out keys that are not yours.
devices.approval.noFingerprint: This browser can't show your account's key fingerprint, so the new device's keys can't be compared with it. Approve from a device that can.
devices.approval.what: Approving sends that device your account key, encrypted to a key it made for this request. The server passes it on without being able to read it. Afterwards the new device shows your account's key fingerprint: compare it with the one at the top of this page.
devices.approval.noKey: The server didn't send this request's key, so this browser can't work out its phrase and won't approve it. Approve it from a Kemlock app, or deny it.
devices.thisBrowser.name: this browser
devices.notListed: This server doesn't list the other apps signed in to your account yet.
devices.trust.onlyThere: Only that device can turn this on: open Kemlock on it.
devices.trusted.label: Trusted device
devices.trusted.body: It keeps a copy of your account key wrapped by a key only it holds, so it can open the vault without the master password.
devices.connect.title: Connect an app or device
devices.connect.lede: Use this server's address in the app, then sign in. A new device may ask you to approve it from one you already use.
devices.connect.failed: Couldn't read this server's address, so there is nothing to copy yet. Close this and try again.
devices.connect.kemlock: Kemlock: Settings, Sync, Kemlock Server, then sign in.
devices.connect.amethystora: Amethystora Vault: the Sync page, with this address as the server.
devices.connect.bitwarden: Bitwarden apps: choose a self-hosted server and paste this address.
security.signedInAs: {email} · signs in with the master password
security.keys.title: Account keys
security.keys.lede: Made on your devices. The server keeps them only wrapped.
security.keys.pairHint: ML-KEM-1024 with X25519 · every item key and space key is sealed to it
security.keys.passwordHint: Argon2id · changing it isn't offered here yet
security.twoStep.title: Two-step login
security.twoStep.appHint: Keep this code outside the vault it protects
security.passkeys.title: Passkeys
security.passkeys.hint: Sign in with one, and confirm admin changes with it. If its authenticator supports PRF it also opens the vault; if not, the master password does.
security.passkeys.proofApp: A second step is on, so adding a passkey asks for a code too. Enter a current code from your authenticator app, or your recovery code. It works once.
security.passkeys.cancelled: The passkey was not made. Try again.
security.passkeys.unavailable: This browser can not make a passkey here. Passkeys need HTTPS or localhost.
security.method.yubikey.hint: Needs a Yubico API key on the server
security.method.duo.hint: Push approval through your Duo account
security.method.email.hint: A code sent to your address
security.method.recovery.hint: Turns two-step login off if every method is lost
security.method.webauthn.hint: A hardware key you touch: up to five
security.proof.sent: To turn this off we mailed a code to your address. Enter it here; it works once. If no mail came, a current code from your authenticator app or your recovery code works too.
security.proof.keyReady: Security key confirmed. It proves it is you for this change.
security.proofAdd.sent: Another second step is on, so adding one asks for a code too. We mailed one to your address; enter it here, it works once. If no mail came, a current code from your authenticator app or your recovery code works too.
security.totp.proof: Another second step is on, so adding an authenticator app asks for a code too. We mailed one to your address; enter it here, it works once. If no mail came, your recovery code works too.
security.recovery.proof: The recovery code can undo your second steps, so showing it asks for a code too. We mailed one to your address; enter it here, it works once. If no mail came, a current code from your authenticator app works.
security.secondSteps.beside: You can keep more than one second step: adding another while one is on asks for a code mailed to you. To change a step, turn it off first (that asks for a code too), then set it up again.
security.webauthn.name: Name for this key
security.webauthn.touch: Your browser asks you to insert the key and touch it.
security.yubikey.notOffered: This server has no Yubico API key, so a YubiKey can not be added.
security.yubikey.how: Put the cursor in a field and touch the key: it types a one-time code. Fill one field for each key, up to five.
security.yubikey.nfc: These keys are read over NFC
security.duo.how: Give the host, integration key and secret key of a Duo Web SDK application. The secret is checked with Duo and kept sealed on the server.
security.duo.howServer: This server has a Duo integration you can use: leave the fields empty. Or give your own host, integration key and secret key.
security.email.notOffered: This server can not send mail, so emailed codes are not offered.
security.recovery.keep: Keep this code where only you can read it, apart from this device. Entering it at the second step turns every method off and uses the code up.
security.recovery.none: This account has no recovery code (it was never made, or it was used).
security.kit.title: Recovery Kit
security.kit.hint: Opens the vault without the master password: any 2 of 3 pieces
security.kit.stale: This kit was made for an older key of your account, so its pieces no longer open the vault. Make a new kit.
security.kit.once: These 3 pieces are shown once, and this server never keeps them. Any 2 open your vault, so keep each in a different place.
security.kit.replaces: Keeping this kit makes every piece of the old kit stop working. We mailed a code to your address; enter it below. It works once.
security.kit.apart: Print them or write them down. Do not keep two pieces together, or in this browser.
security.kit.confirm: Type any one piece to show you kept it
security.kit.mismatch: That is not one of the pieces above. Check it against the page.
security.kit.keep: I kept them: turn the kit on
security.kit.keepNew: I kept them: replace the old kit
security.kit.removeBody: Without a kit, only your master password, an approval from another device or a passkey opens your vault. The pieces you hold stop working.
security.kit.proofSent: We mailed a code to your address. Enter it here; it works once. If no mail came, a current code from your authenticator app or your recovery code works too.
security.apiKey.title: API key
security.apiKey.hint: For the Bitwarden CLI and scripts: sign in with the client id and secret, without your master password or second step.
security.apiKey.unavailable: This account signs in only through Kemlock, so it has no API key. Accounts made through the Bitwarden-compatible sign-in have one.
security.apiKey.hidden: Kept hidden. Showing it asks for a fresh code.
security.apiKey.notMade: Not made yet. The first ask makes it, with a fresh code.
security.apiKey.proofBody: The secret opens the account without its second step, so showing it asks for a code too.
security.apiKey.rotateBody: A new secret replaces the old one at once: every script that signs in with the old secret stops working until you give it the new one.
security.apiKey.created: The key is made. Keep the secret where only you and your scripts can read it.
security.apiKey.rotated: The secret was replaced. The old secret no longer signs in.
security.apiKey.keep: Anyone with this secret can open the account. Hide it when you are done.
security.signed.title: Signed writes only
security.signed.hint: Refuse any change to your vault that is not signed by this account, here and on every server that holds it
security.signed.warnOn: Turn it on once every device you use signs its changes. A device that doesn't sign yet is refused while it is on.
security.signed.warnOff: While it is on, nobody who only has your session can write to your vault without your keys. Turning it off lets unsigned changes in again.
security.delete.title: Delete account
security.delete.hint: Erases the account, its vault and its devices
security.delete.warn: This erases your vault, its files, your Sends, your devices and sessions, your second steps, passkeys, emergency contacts and recovery kit. It cannot be undone.
security.delete.spaces: You leave every space you are in. If you are the only owner of a space that others are still in, hand it over or delete it first.
security.delete.lastOwner: You are the only owner of a space with other members. Hand it over to another owner, or delete the space, then try again.
twoStep.scanTitle: Add this account to your authenticator app
twoStep.scan: Scan the code with your authenticator app. It will list {email} under {host}.
twoStep.typeKey: Or type this key into the app:
twoStep.typeCode: Then type the 6 digits the app shows.
twoStep.keepApp: Keep the app somewhere other than this vault.
emergency.title: Emergency access
emergency.lede: Someone you trust can ask for your vault. You have the wait time to refuse.
emergency.line: {kind} · waits {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
emergency.due: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} left
emergency.confirm.title: Confirm {name}
emergency.confirm.body: Confirming seals your account key to {name}'s keys. Ask them to read out the numbers their app shows, and check they match:
emergency.released.title: {name}'s key was released
emergency.released.view: It lets you view their vault. Opening it takes this browser's key worker, which can't yet.
emergency.released.takeover: It lets you take over their account. Opening it takes this browser's key worker, which can't yet.
security.rotate.title: Rotate account keys
security.rotate.hint: Makes a new root key for your account, so an old Recovery Kit, device copy or emergency contact's key opens nothing new
security.rotate.what: This makes a new root key and a new key pair, encrypts every item and Send again under them, and deletes every copy of the old root key on this server, in one step. If anything fails, nothing changes.
security.rotate.others: Every other device is signed out and has to sign in again.
security.rotate.passkeys: {n, plural, one {# passkey stops opening the vault; set it up again under Passkeys.} other {# passkeys stop opening the vault; set them up again under Passkeys.}}
security.rotate.emergency: {n, plural, one {# emergency contact is kept only if you compare their fingerprint below; otherwise you confirm them again later.} other {# emergency contacts are kept only if you compare their fingerprints below; otherwise you confirm them again later.}}
security.rotate.asContact: {n, plural, one {# person named you as their emergency contact: they confirm you again, to your new keys.} other {# people named you as their emergency contact: they confirm you again, to your new keys.}}
security.rotate.contact: Keep {email} as an emergency contact: I compared this fingerprint with the one on their own screen
security.rotate.recovery: {n, plural, one {# space recovery enrolment is removed unless this browser can check its space's recovery key; enrol again.} other {# space recovery enrolments are removed unless this browser can check their spaces' recovery keys; enrol again.}}
security.rotate.files: Files attached to items keep their own keys. Replace a file if you must treat its old key as known.
security.rotate.kitReplace: Replace my Recovery Kit with a new one (the old pieces stop working)
security.rotate.done: The keys were rotated. Your new fingerprint is {fingerprint}.
security.rotate.removed: Removed: {passkeys, plural, one {# passkey wrap} other {# passkey wraps}}, {emergency, plural, one {# emergency contact box} other {# emergency contact boxes}}, {recovery, plural, one {# recovery enrolment} other {# recovery enrolments}}. Set them up again.
security.rotate.blocked.spaces: You belong to a shared space, whose keys must move to the new keys too. The web vault can't do that yet: rotate your keys from the Kemlock app, or leave the space first and rotate here.
security.rotate.blocked.compatible: This account is shared with Bitwarden apps, which hold its root key, so its keys can't be rotated here.
security.rotate.readd.hint: Rotation removed this passkey's unlock of the vault. Touch it to add it back.
security.rotate.error.incomplete: Your account kept changing while the keys were being rotated, so nothing was changed. Try again when your other devices are quiet.
security.rotate.blocked.federated: This account's vault is held on other servers too, which a rotation here can't reach, so its keys can't be rotated.
security.rotate.passkeyOnly: This account has no master password. Touch a passkey or security key to prove it is you.
security.rotate.needPasskey: This account has no master password. Add a passkey or security key first: a session alone can't rotate its keys.
security.rotate.failedAfter: The keys were rotated on the server, but this browser could not finish. Your other devices and this one are signed out: sign in again. Keep the new Recovery Kit below.
security.rotate.error.proof: Your account changed while the keys were being rotated, so nothing was changed and the code you gave may be spent. Get a new one and try again.
security.rotate.error.items: An item of your vault can't be rotated here. Nothing was changed.
